A_target.statement:
Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be [[Definition:Independent Identically Distributed|i.i.d.]] with [[Definition:Distribution|distribution]] $P$ on a [[Definition:Finite Set|finite]] alphabet $\XX$ and [[Definition:Entropy (Information Theory)|entropy]] $\map H P$.
Let $\epsilon > 0$.
Then for sufficiently large $n$ the [[Definition:Typical Set|typical set]] $A_\epsilon^{\paren n}$ satisfies:
:$\map \Pr {A_\epsilon^{\paren n} } > 1 - \epsilon$
and:
:$\size {A_\epsilon^{\paren n} } \le 2^{n \paren {\map H P + \epsilon} }$

B_source.statement:
Let $n = n_1 + n_2 + \cdots + n_k$.
Then the number of sequences of length $n$ over an alphabet of $k$ symbols in which symbol $i$ occurs exactly $n_i$ times is the [[Definition:Multinomial Coefficient|multinomial coefficient]]:
:$\dbinom n {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} = \dfrac {n!} {n_1! \, n_2! \cdots n_k!}$

substitutions.the sequences with prescribed symbol cou: the sequences whose empirical distribution matches the source
substitutions.the multinomial coefficient counting the: the size of the typical set
substitutions.the exponential growth rate of that coef: the entropy of the source distribution

derived.the Stirling estimate of the multinomial: growth at the rate given by the entropy
derived.the probability of the matching frequenc: tending to one by the law of large numbers

object_map.reformulation: Replace the probabilistic statement by a count of sequences in each empirical frequency class.

validity_conditions: The number of empirical frequency classes grows only polynomially in the sequence length, while each class has exponential size, so one class dominates.
Stirling's estimate converts the multinomial coefficient into an exponential whose rate is the entropy of the empirical distribution.
The law of large numbers makes the empirical distribution converge to the source distribution, so the dominant class is the one matching it and carries probability tending to one.
proof_plan: Partition $\XX^n$ into [[Definition:Type Class|type classes]] $\map T Q$ according to the [[Definition:Empirical Distribution|empirical distribution]] $Q$ of each sequence.

From the source result:
:$\size {\map T Q} = \dbinom n {n \map Q {a_1}, \ldots, n \map Q {a_k} }$
Applying [[Stirling's Formula]]:
:$\displaystyle \frac 1 n \log_2 \size {\map T Q} \to \map H Q$

Hence the number of sequences of type $Q$ grows as $2^{n \map H Q + \map o n}$.
As there are at most $\paren {n + 1}^{\size \XX}$ types, the growth rate is governed by the [[Definition:Entropy (Information Theory)|entropy]].
